name: James
intro: James writes with prophetic urgency, calling believers to faith that produces works. Often called the Proverbs of the New Testament, James addresses practical wisdom for living as God's people: controlling the tongue, caring for the poor, resisting favoritism, and enduring trials with joy.

themes.title: Faith and works
themes.body: Faith without works is dead. Genuine faith produces obedience, just as Abraham's faith was completed by his works. James does not contradict Paul but insists that true faith always bears fruit in action.

themes.title: Trials and perseverance
themes.body: Count it all joy when you meet trials, for testing produces steadfastness. Blessed is the one who remains steadfast under trial, for when tested he will receive the crown of life.

themes.title: The tongue and wisdom
themes.body: The tongue is a small member yet boasts great things. No human can tame the tongue, a restless evil full of deadly poison. Wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits.

themes.title: Care for the vulnerable
themes.body: Pure religion is to visit orphans and widows in their affliction and to keep oneself unstained from the world. Show no partiality, for God has chosen the poor to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom.

themes.title: Prayer and humility
themes.body: The prayer of a righteous person has great power. Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.

structure.title: Trials, Wisdom, and Temptation (1)
structure.body: Joy in trials, asking for wisdom, and being doers of the word.

structure.title: Favoritism and Faith (2)
structure.body: Show no partiality, love your neighbor, faith without works is dead.

structure.title: The Tongue and Wisdom (3)
structure.body: Taming the tongue and wisdom from above versus earthly wisdom.

structure.title: Submission and Patience (4–5)
structure.body: Submit to God, resist the devil, patience in suffering, and prayer for healing.

whyRead: James provides practical wisdom for Christian living with prophetic directness. Its emphasis on faith that produces works, care for the poor, and the power of prayer makes it essential for understanding how doctrine translates into practice.
